photovoltaic-effect.short: Light falling on a material produces a voltage and can drive a current, with no moving parts. It is how every solar cell works.

photoconductivity.short: A material conducts electricity better when light shines on it, because light frees extra charge carriers. It needs an outside battery; it does not make power by itself.

photoelectric-effect.short: Light knocks electrons out of a metal surface. Einstein explained it in 1905 by treating light as packets (photons), each with energy set by its colour.

czochralski-process.short: A way to grow one large, nearly flawless crystal: dip a small seed crystal into molten material and pull it up slowly while turning it. Most single-crystal silicon is made this way.

feed-in-tariff.short: A law that guarantees a fixed price, for many years, for each kilowatt-hour a renewable generator feeds into the grid. It makes small and large projects easy to finance.
